simple.meaning: צָעַד (tsâʻad) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to pace , i.e. step regularly ; (upward) to mount ; (along) to march ; (down and causatively) to hurl.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 8 times across Genesis, Judges, 2 Samuel, Job, Psalms, and 3 more, beginning at Genesis 49:22. Its contexts include sacrifice.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to צָעַד (H6805).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: צָעַד (tsâʻad) / H6805 is traced through Genesis 49:22, Judges 5:4, 2 Samuel 6:13, Job 18:14 as a generated source-based concept entry.

occurrences.englishText: “Yahweh, when you went out of Seir,
When those who bore Yahweh’s ark had gone six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened calf.
He will be rooted out of the security of his tent.
passing through the street near her corner,
They are like a palm tree, of turned work,
You marched through the land in wrath.
